where: Section 3, first paragraph and the key-turn sequence
problem: The control circuit is said to carry 'a few amperes', but three lines later the same circuit carries the pull-in and hold-in coils at 'about 40 A in total' (and about 10 A when held). A student is left with two contradictory current values for one conductor. 40 A is not a few amperes, and that coil current flows through the terminal 50 line, the relay contact and any safety switch in it.
fix: Say: the relay coil side of the control circuit carries only 0.1 A to 0.3 A; the terminal 50 line that feeds the solenoid coils carries about 40 A while the plunger is moving and about 10 A once the main contacts close. Both are small compared with the 150 A to 400 A of the power circuit, but they are not the same current.

where: Section 3, second bullet of the key-turn sequence
problem: 'Battery voltage reaches terminal 50 of the starter relay coil' mixes two nodes. Terminal 50 is the starter control line at the solenoid. The relay coil is fed from the ignition switch (terminal 15 side), and the relay contact feeds terminal 50 of the solenoid.
fix: Write: the ignition switch feeds the relay coil; the relay contact then feeds terminal 50 of the solenoid.

problem: 'Four starter motor arrangements' is ambiguous, because the chapter also describes four drive arrangements (Bendix, pre-engaged, overrunning clutch, armature shift). A student cannot tell which list is wanted.
fix: Ask: 'List the four starter motor types described in Section 1.' Keep the answer as series-wound, permanent-magnet, gear-reduction and coaxial.

problem: The power is found from the terminal voltage at the starter (10.5 V) and is then called 'energy taken from the battery'. The battery actually supplies more, because of its internal resistance and the cable drop; 5250 J is the energy delivered to the starter.
fix: Say: 2625 W is the power delivered to the starter and 5250 J the energy it takes, measured at its terminals. The battery must supply slightly more because of internal and cable losses.
